progression

/pro-GRESH-un/ — rhymes with fashion · noun

Hear It

What It Means

A progression is a step-by-step development from one stage to the next.

Watching this progression from egg to caterpillar to winged insect, students could hardly believe that all four forms belonged to a single living thing.

Worked Example

Over the spring, Maya's artwork showed an amazing progression: her first painting was muddy and flat, her second had better colors, and her third showed real perspective.

Progression emphasizes the step-by-step, orderly nature of the change—each stage leads logically to the next. If we just said 'improvement,' we'd miss the sense that each stage is a necessary building block.

Compare the words

Synonyms · words with a similar meaning

sequence: A sequence is items in a fixed order — steps, numbers, scenes — with nothing said about growth between them. A progression is a sequence with development inside it: each stage builds on the one before and leads to the next. A playlist is a sequence; a course of lessons where each builds on the last is a progression.

evolution: Evolution is gradual change that emerges on its own, without a plan or fixed stages — tastes evolve, cities evolve. A progression moves through recognizable stages in order, each preparing the next. If you can number the steps, it is a progression; if the change simply accumulated, it is an evolution.

escalation: An escalation is a step-by-step rise in intensity or stakes, almost always of something unwelcome — an escalation of a conflict, of prices. A progression is the neutral word for staged development of any kind. Piano exercises form a progression; threats trading back and forth form an escalation.

What it isn’t · antonyms and near-opposites

regression: slipping backward to an earlier stage

standstill: a complete halt with no movement

Where it sits · how connected the forward steps are — stagnation → change → advancement → progression

stagnation vs. progression: A pond's stagnation means nothing moves or develops at all — the weakest state on this scale — while progression describes active, ordered movement from one stage to the next.

change vs. progression: Change claims only that something is different now — a repainted bedroom is a change — but progression is stronger, requiring a connected series of stages that build on one another.

advancement vs. progression: An intern's advancement to a paid position marks one forward jump, but progression makes the stronger claim of a whole staircase of stages, each one preparing the way for the next.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pro-

Prefix — pro-: forward

Root — gress-

Root — gress-: to step (Latin gradi, which shifts its spelling among grad-, gred-, and -gress- as it moves through English)

Suffix — -ion

Suffix — -ion: act or process of

Put it together

Put it together: Pro- (forward) + gress- (to step — Latin gradi, which shifts its spelling among grad-, gred-, and -gress- as it moves through English) + -ion (act or process of) = the act of stepping forward — movement onward, one step at a time. That spelling shift is why progression's close cousin is progress, while gradual keeps the grad- form.

Use the root in a new word: digress

Use the root in a new word: digress: When the teacher started to digress about her childhood, the students had to remind her to return to the algebra lesson.

Word Choice

neutral / academic

Use progression when describing a step-by-step, orderly change where each stage is necessary and builds toward the next. For a simple list of things in order with no development between them, use succession instead.
